reason: The passage extensively emphasizes hierarchical relationships and obedience to authority. God commands Abraham with absolute authority (וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים), and Abraham responds with immediate submission (וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּנִי - 'Here I am'). Abraham then exercises authority over his servants, commanding them to remain behind (שְׁבוּ־ לָכֶם פֹּה עִם־ הַחֲמוֹר), and over his son Isaac. The narrative structure emphasizes obedience to higher authority: Abraham's willingness to obey God's command is presented as the ultimate test of devotion, and this obedience is explicitly rewarded with divine blessing and covenant renewal. The angel's affirmation ('now I know that you fear God, and you have not withheld your son') validates the hierarchical submission. The entire passage valorizes the submission of lower hierarchical levels to higher ones, with obedience to authority portrayed as virtuous and rewarded.
